transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today? How can I help you?

I came in because this has gotten hard to manage. When I’m driving and my car gets to one of those long bridges toward Miami, right away my chest tightens, my hands grip the steering wheel, and I just get this sudden feeling that I have to get off the bridge immediately—even though there’s nowhere to go.
Do these feelings of chest tightness and urgency happen in other situations, or only when you're driving on bridges?

It’s really when I’m driving on those long bridges. The moment my car gets onto one heading toward Miami, my chest tightens, my hands clamp down on the wheel, and I get this sudden feeling like I have to get off right away, even though I know there’s nowhere to go.
Do you experience similar feelings of chest tightening or urgency in other situations, like tunnels, highways, or even when you're not driving at all?

Not really that I’ve noticed. It’s that bridge situation—when my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami. Right away my chest tightens, my hands clamp down on the wheel, and I feel sure I need to get off, even though there’s nowhere to get off.

Do you ever experience similar panic-like symptoms in other situations, such as flying, enclosed spaces, or during public speaking, or is this something that only happens when you're on those bridges toward Miami?

It seems to be just those bridges toward Miami. I don’t get that same feeling with other things. It’s really the moment my car reaches one of those long bridges—my chest tightens, my hands clamp the wheel, and I’m suddenly sure I need to get off, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Have you ever had a sudden surge of fear or panic in any other specific situations, even if it wasn't while driving or on a bridge?

No, I can’t think of another specific situation where it happens like that. It’s really when my car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami—then my chest tightens, my hands grip the wheel, and I get this sudden feeling that I have to get off, even though there isn’t anywhere to go.
Have you ever had a reaction like this—racing heart, chest tightness, or a sudden need to escape—when you're not in the car or not near a bridge?

No, not really. I don’t get that when I’m just at home or out somewhere. It’s when I’m driving and the car reaches one of those long bridges toward Miami—then my chest tightens and I feel like I have to get off right away, even though I can’t.
Have you ever had a panic attack or similar physical symptoms in any other specific phobic situations, like flying, elevators, or enclosed spaces?

No, I don’t think so. Not flying or elevators or places like that. It’s really that moment when my car gets onto one of those long bridges toward Miami—my chest tightens, my hands lock onto the wheel, and I just feel certain I need to get off, even though there’s nowhere to go.

When you feel that sudden urge to get off the bridge, do you feel like something bad is going to happen to you if you stay on the bridge, like you might panic, lose control, or have a medical problem?

Yes… in that moment it feels like I have to get off the bridge right away. My chest tightens and my hands clamp onto the wheel, and I get this sudden certainty that I can’t stay there, even though there’s nowhere to go.
Do you go out of your way to avoid driving on those bridges toward Miami, or do you still drive on them even though it causes you a lot of distress?

Yes. I’ve started avoiding them when I can. I turn down gallery openings, birdwatching trips, even some visits with my daughter unless someone else can drive me over those bridges. It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’ve always been the one who planned things and handled the driving myself.
